chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya'qub from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:

"When the Maghrib prayer is performed in fear, they are divided into two groups. The Imam prays with one group for two rak'ahs, then sits with them, then gestures to them with his hand, so each person stands up and prays one rak'ah, then they say the Taslim. They stand in the place of their companions, and the other group comes forward, says Takbir, and enters the prayer. The Imam stands and prays one rak'ah with them, then says Taslim. Then each man from them stands and prays one rak'ah, completing it with the one he prayed with the Imam. Then he stands and prays one rak'ah in which there is no recitation, so it is completed for the Imam three rak'ahs, and for the first group two rak'ahs in congregation, and for the latter group individually. Thus, for the first group is the Takbir and the opening of the prayer, and for the latter group is the Taslim."

key_terms.اِلْتِقَاطُ: Completing/collecting (implied context of completing the prayer)

ai.seo_question: How is the Maghrib prayer performed in two parts during times of fear according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the detailed mechanics of Salat al-Khawf for Maghrib, where the congregation splits into two groups to maintain vigilance. The Imam leads the first group through two rak'ahs, after which they complete the prayer individually while the second group joins him for the final rak'ah, ensuring the full prayer is performed by all. This method highlights the Shia emphasis on maintaining both ritual completeness and tactical readiness during conflict.
